meta.parties: Sadris Appu Et Al. v. Cornelis Appu Et Al

rules.statement: Execution-creditors who allow their own property to be sold as the property of an execution-debtor under a writ over which they have control are estopped from later claiming that the property was theirs and not the debtor's.
rules.supporting_quote: "It appears to me clear that the appellants, who actually permitted their own property to be seized and sold under their own writ, over which writ they had absolute control, as the property of the first defendant, cannot be allowed now to say against the purchaser, the second defendant, or his vendee, the first defendant, that the property seized and sold under their writ was their property and not the property of the first defendant."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: "when one person has by his declaration act, or omission intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed in any suit or proceeding between himself and such person or his representative to deny the truth of that thing."
